name: Italy CPI Headline YoY (NIC, all items)
notes: ISTAT SDMX dataflow 167_745_DF_DCSP_NIC1B2025_6 'Consumer prices for the whole nation (Nic) — monthly data - all bases', key M.IT..7.00 = FREQ Monthly / REF_AREA IT / DATA_TYPE wildcard / MEASURE 7 ('percentage changes on the same period of the previous year') / ECOICOP_2 00 (all items). Registered 2026-07-30 as the national-primary ITA_CPI_YOY, displacing a DB.nomics relay of OECD COICOP2018 (third-hand). The DATA_TYPE wildcard is deliberate: the 'all bases' flow splits the series across four disjoint base periods (1 = base 1995 for 1997-01->2010-12, 9 = base 2010 for 2011-01->2015-12, 39 = base 2015 for 2016-01->2025-12, 85 = base 2025 for 2026-01->), and the wildcard is what makes it one continuous series — pinning any single DATA_TYPE would truncate it. FRAGILITY: this relies on _rows_to_obs' first-wins period dedupe, which is only safe because the four segments are disjoint today; if ISTAT ever publishes overlapping bases the chosen value would be arbitrary. Verified live 2026-07-30 through sources/istat.py: 354 obs 1997-01 -> 2026-06 = 3.0, 2 MONTHS FRESHER than the relay (2026-04). The relay stays tier 1 and extends the head 1956-01 -> 1996-12 under C16 (+41 years, seam 0.0498pp). Same trade as CAN_CPI_YOY: ISTAT publishes to 1 decimal (the canonical figure), the relay to full precision, hence the 0.0498pp = half-a-rounding-unit spread — pure rounding, not methodology. See forward_plan §2.C C16.1.
